name: GameAssist
description:
**GameAssist is a modular D&D 5E automation suite for Roll20. Its critical-miss, condition, concentration, token, NPC, effect, healing, guided-attack, reporting, configuration, and diagnostic tools support the 2014 sheet; InitiativeAssist adds mixed 2014 and 2024 initiative in Roll20's native Turn Tracker; CombatAssist provides deliberate encounter, turn, and round controls; WelcomeAssist can open game night with a table greeting chosen by the GM; and AlmanacAssist joins fictional time, coherent current scenes, campaign travel, worldbuilding, weather, environments, and deliberate rests.**

GameAssist v2.0.0 includes fifteen individually configurable modules supported by shared MarkerService, TurnTrackerService, HealthService, and versioned semantic-event foundations. HealthService can also provide optional GM-private PC health alerts at selected health bands. Guided menus and plain-language help make the common workflows approachable, while direct commands and deeper controls remain available when a campaign needs them. Every module treats its `GM` and `DM` commands as equal shortcuts to that module's primary private Game Master screen. The suite navigator gives every running module a direct Disable control and every off module an Enable control. GameAssist command words ignore capitalization and accept either spaces or hyphens, while shared control panels use one consistent Roll20 template style.

Campaigns upgrading from v0.1.7.0 keep their established commands, valid settings, NPC history, Arc records, and guide handouts. The canonical module names are now **CritAssist**, **NPCAssist**, **ConcentrationAssist**, and **HPAssist**; legacy command forms remain available for existing macros.

---

## ⚙️ Requirements

- **Roll20 access:** Mod scripts require a game created by a Roll20 Pro subscriber. Players in that game do not need their own Pro subscriptions.
- **Character sheets:** EffectAssist, HealAssist, AttackAssist, RestAlmanac, and the established gameplay modules use D&D 5E by Roll20 (2014). InitiativeAssist supports both 2014 and D&D 2024 by Roll20 characters in the same encounter. Time, Climate, Astronomy, Weather, and Environment do not require a character sheet. Roll20's supported Experimental Mod API server may be needed for 2024 Beacon initiative data.
- **Integrated services:** Remove standalone TokenMod and StatusInfo before normal v2.0.0 use. TokenAssist and ConditionAssist provide the supported integrated replacements, and MarkerService owns their shared marker behavior.
- **NPC tokens:** NPCAssist and HPAssist use the shared NPC HP bar selected through `!ga-health bars` (Bar 1, 2, or 3). Tokens must be on the Objects layer, linked to a character with `npc=1`, and need `npc_hpformula` when GameAssist rolls their HP.
- **CritAssist tables:** `CF-Melee`, `CF-Ranged`, `CF-Thrown`, `CF-Spell`, `CF-Natural`, `Confirm-Crit-Martial`, and `Confirm-Crit-Magic`

> GameAssist does not invent your campaign's fumble results. Create and populate the seven rollable tables before using CritAssist table rolls.

> TokenAssist uses `!token-assist` and `!ta`/`!ta-*` commands. Older supported `!token-mod` macros remain compatibility aliases in v2.0.0. Use `!token-assist` or `!ta` for new macros; any later removal will be announced through a separate migration release.

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

GameAssist is controlled from Roll20 chat. Commands beginning with `!` are sent to Mods instead of appearing as ordinary chat messages; players do not install anything separately.

1. From the game's **Settings**, open **Mod (API) Scripts** and add **GameAssist** from the One-Click library.
2. Remove standalone TokenMod and StatusInfo so overlapping commands and marker listeners are not loaded twice.
3. Create the seven CritAssist rollable tables if you plan to use CritAssist.
4. Allow the Mod sandbox to restart, then type `!ga-status` in chat to check the installation.
5. Run `!ga-timezone` and choose the city/region that governs the campaign clock.
6. Open `!ga-config ui` and enable only the modules your campaign needs.
7. When using native initiative tools, enable **InitiativeAssist**, open Roll20's Turn Tracker, and run `!Init-Help`.
8. To track encounter turns and rounds, enable **CombatAssist**, establish initiative, then run `!Combat-Help` before starting the encounter.
9. For an optional table greeting, enable **WelcomeAssist**, run `!Welcome`, preview the result, then reload the sandbox.
10. To coordinate spell effects, enable **EffectAssist**, select disposable linked 2014-sheet targets, run `!effect`, choose the source, and confirm the effect works on the first supported roll. Application Review is optional and starts off.
11. To guide healing, enable **HealAssist**, damage a disposable linked 2014 PC, and run `!Heal`. Review-before-apply is the default; `!Heal-Max` opens maximum healing, and the GM may deliberately enable automatic verified application.
12. To guide a 2014-sheet attack, enable **AttackAssist**, select a controlled linked PC, run `!Attack`, and choose one repeating attack and visible target.
13. To manage the campaign world, enable **AlmanacAssist** and open `!aa-gm` for the compact Current World screen. Use `!aa-world` only when building places, natural-world definitions, local contexts, presets, or transfer packages.

Use `!Init-Help`, `!Combat-Help`, `!Welcome`, `!token-assist help`, `!condition help`, `!critfumble help`, `!concentration --help`, `!npc-death-report --help`, `!Effect-Guide`, `!Heal-Guide`, `!Attack-Guide`, or `!Almanac-Guide` whenever you want an in-game guide.

## 🧩 Included Modules

- **CritAssist** — Watches supported attack templates for natural 1s, offers the attacker clear choices, and rolls from your melee, ranged, thrown, spell, or natural-attack fumble tables. The GM can also open a player picker manually or roll martial and magic confirmation tables directly.
- **ConditionAssist** — Uses 2014 SRD condition wording by default, offers optional 2024 SRD wording and campaign edits, and provides case-insensitive `!cond-<condition>` quick references, marker artwork, an accurate selected-token condition menu, a GM current-page condition/marker status roster, and verified marker-toggling announcements in public chat or player whispers. Valid legacy StatusInfo definitions can be copied without deleting the rollback state.
- **TokenAssist** — Provides bare `!token`, full-name `!tokenassist`, `!token-assist`, and `!ta`/`!ta-*` token controls for selected or authorized tokens. It handles common visibility settings, names, tooltips, bars, auras, colors, layers, position, size, rotation, vision, lighting, links, controllers, relative values, movement, stacking order, reports, and built-in or custom status markers. Marker changes always pass through MarkerService.
- **InitiativeAssist** — Works inside Roll20's native Turn Tracker with mixed 2014 and 2024 characters. Public initiative calls offer one-character, selected-character, and guided roll buttons while privately giving the GM object-layer and GM-layer NPC controls. `!Init-GM` and `!Init-DM` open the same neutral controls and complete roster only for the GM. NPC roll details are hidden by default, GM-layer rolls always stay private, and guided options combine d20 mode, a flat adjustment, and up to two bonus dice. `!Init-RR` whispers the GM a bounded result summary while preserving custom counters, objects, dead NPCs, mismatches, stale rows, and off-page entries.
- **CombatAssist** — Adds an optional encounter layer to Roll20's native Turn Tracker without replacing it. A clearly named native Round Counter can provide the authoritative round and retain its simple `+1` calculation during CombatAssist movement. The GM starts, reviews, moves forward or backward, pauses when useful, and ends tracking through a case-insensitive `!Combat-` guide. Valid combatant additions, removals, rerolls, and manual reordering preserve the current round. Optional turn timers provide stale-safe reminders without auto-advancing, and native current-turn pings add an ephemeral visual cue without changing token properties or recentering anyone's map. Private turn prompts can give the current controlling player an End My Turn button followed by a privacy-safe confirmation.
- **WelcomeAssist** — Starts disabled and optionally posts one delayed greeting after a healthy GameAssist startup. The GM can choose the professional greeting, the included built-in greeting library, up to ten campaign greetings, or a mixed pool that gives campaign lines double individual weight. Setup and previews stay private; automatic and explicit announcements are public.
- **ConcentrationAssist** — Builds normal, advantage, or disadvantage Constitution saves from verified official-2014 Constitution save data, remembers each player's latest check, manages a concentration marker through MarkerService, lists concentrating tokens on the Player Ribbon page, and provides the lifecycle contract used by concentration-dependent EffectAssist records. Missing Classic data and recognized 2024 Beacon characters receive a clear native-sheet fallback instead of a guessed `+0`. With HealthService enabled, supported HP loss can offer one private, revalidated check to the GM and eligible controllers without claiming that an unexplained decrease has a known cause. Fresh campaigns use Roll20's built-in stopwatch marker; the GM can choose another built-in or registered custom marker from ConcentrationAssist Settings.
- **NPCAssist** — Marks defeated NPCs, records revivals, checks HP against death markers, previews separately confirmed marker repairs, and organizes encounter history into readable handouts using **Campaign > Chapter > Section > Session** scopes. Custom Arc rosters can follow NPCs connected to a character story, vow, rivalry, investigation, redemption, or any other campaign thread. Date-managed Sessions and readable history use the DM-selected table timezone. Optional automatic naming gives newly added linked NPC tokens unique page-local names without renaming existing tokens or characters. Optional Bloodied alerts privately notify the GM when an eligible living NPC crosses to half HP or below without adding a marker or history entry.
- **EffectAssist** — Starts disabled and coordinates a focused six-effect catalog for the official 2014 sheet. Bless, Guidance, Warding Bond, and Haste apply supported marker and sheet automation with compact `(GA)` modifier labels; Holy Weapon and Pass Without a Trace are visibly labeled tracked effects whose rule mechanics remain manual. Supported effects apply after source selection by default, while the GM can enable Application Review. New concentration normally replaces the source's prior effect; an advanced setting can permit exceptional multiple-concentration campaigns. Player casting asks for the caster first and the recipient count second. Bless offers one to three recipients directly plus Higher Level Casting choices for four through eleven; invalid recipients are named precisely, unique caster choices stay compact, duplicate caster labels add concise token and layer details, and hidden or off-page recipients can be sent to a retained private GM request. An unambiguous official 2014 Bless card can create a private GM proposal without choosing recipients or applying anything automatically. Concentration-dependent effects validate the campaign marker before any recipient marker or sheet row is written. Optional CombatAssist rounds and Almanac time can flag a duration for private GM review without ending the effect automatically. Concentration belongs to the exact chosen source token. Overlap, pre-existing state, externally edited rows, audits, repairs, cast proposals, and duration decisions use ownership evidence rather than guesswork, and cleanup names campaign state it deliberately preserves.
- **HealAssist** — Starts disabled and guides official-2014 healing through supported spells, potions, or a bounded manual formula. Normal and maximum-healing catalogs are available. Review-before-apply is the default; the GM may enable automatic verified application after recipient selection, and failed automatic writes produce a private GM diagnostic. Players may target visible supported PCs without gaining token control; NPC, GM-layer, hidden, and off-page placement remains private and GM-reviewed. Spell slots, items, class resources, and temporary HP remain table responsibilities.
- **AttackAssist** — Starts disabled and guides an authorized official-2014 PC through one exact repeating attack, a compact native visible-target choice, and the sheet, Normal, Advantage, or Disadvantage roll mode. Explicit modes materialize documented Classic-sheet defaults, including the ordinary critical range and attack, damage, second-damage, and save checkbox values, rather than requiring hidden attributes such as `d20`, `atkcritrange`, `atkflag`, `dmgflag`, `dmg2flag`, or `saveflag`; genuinely unknown missing fields are refused before submission. Duplicate attack names retain separate stable row identities; hidden or off-page placement stays in a private GM request. AttackAssist sends the familiar character-attributed attack card directly through Roll20, then gives one compact submission notice; it never applies damage, spends resources, or changes encounter state.
- **AlmanacAssist** - Starts disabled and separates live play from campaign construction. `!aa-gm` opens a compact Current World screen for place, coherent scene, time, date, travel, rest, weather, announcements, and quick actions; `!aa-world` opens the grouped worldbuilding workspace. Six independently controlled Time, Climate, Astronomy, Weather, Environment, and Rest systems feed one provenance-bearing SceneResolver without becoming hidden prerequisites. Bounded geographies, biomes, ecoregions, locations, phenomena, local temporal contexts, and prepared destinations support reviewed travel and reusable campaign setup. The advanced Wayfarer handout replaces only an unreviewed saved draft, while versioned WorldPacks validate the complete definition graph and exclude runtime chronology and character state. Optional RulesAdvisor guidance never applies gameplay changes. Existing Wayfarer clocks, announcement levels, moon visibility, environment overrides, recovery, and transactional 2014-sheet rests remain available.
- **HPAssist** — Rolls `npc_hpformula` for selected NPCs or qualifying NPCs on the page marked by Roll20's Player Ribbon and writes the shared NPC HP bar selected through `!ga-health bars`. Optional automatic rolling handles newly added tokens while setup protection prevents placeholder HP from producing false death, revival, or Bloodied events. HealthService records supported HPAssist writes as verified initialization or synchronization evidence.
- **ConfigUI** — Provides a GM-only chat interface for enabling components, changing common settings, reviewing alphabetized Services and Modules, reading compact wrapping summaries instead of raw nested data, and opening protected PC health-alert controls. Command-based configuration and the complete configuration snapshot remain available for advanced users.
- **DebugTools** — Provides optional GM-only damage, marker, and saving-throw diagnostics. DebugTools starts disabled, every action remains a preview until the GM includes `--apply`, and supported applied damage uses verified HealthService evidence.

---

## 🎲 Example at the Table

A linked NPC falls from positive HP to 0. NPCAssist records that death in the active Campaign, Chapter, Section, and Session scopes, then asks MarkerService to apply the configured death marker. If the NPC later rises above 0 HP, GameAssist records the revival and removes the marker through the same service.

The GM can review a recent summary, audit the current page, write polished records to campaign handouts, or collect selected NPCs into a custom Arc roster. When a token needs an adjustment outside those automated workflows, TokenAssist can change the selected token without introducing a second marker system.

Before a new encounter, the GM opens Roll20's Turn Tracker and uses `!Init-Go` to invite players to roll, or `!Init-GM` / `!Init-DM` to keep the opening controls private. Players can roll one controlled character, every selected character they control, or a guided combination of d20 mode, adjustment, and bonus dice. The GM receives private controls for object-layer and GM-layer NPCs; hidden NPC modifiers and bonus dice remain GM-only. After each page-owned row is saved and verified, the appropriate audience sees the readable result. Later, `!Init-RR` can refresh every PC and living NPC without moving a round counter, object, dead creature, or attention row.

When the cleric blesses several allies, the player chooses a controlled caster and visible recipients through the guided Bless path; a hidden or off-page recipient can be sent to the GM as a retained private request. The GM can instead start Bless directly from the EffectAssist controls. A supported official 2014 Bless card may give the GM a private shortcut, but the GM still selects the actual recipients. After source selection, the targets receive their Blessed markers and active `Bless (GA)` `1d4` attack/save rows while the cleric begins concentrating; an optional setting adds a separate review first. A second Bless source shares those non-stacking projections without taking over the first. Ending concentration removes only the final unneeded EffectAssist-owned state; matching markers or modifier rows that existed first remain. If a verified CombatAssist or Almanac boundary is reached first, the GM receives a private review choice while Bless remains active.

When an ally needs healing, an authorized player or GM opens `!Heal` for normal healing or `!Heal-Max` for the maximum possible result. Review-before-apply is the default; the GM may enable automatic verified application. NPC and hidden work stays private, and the table marks off any spell slot, potion, or feature manually.

When that character attacks, the player can open `!Attack`, choose the exact saved repeating attack, point at a visible map target, and use the sheet setting or an explicit d20 mode. The ordinary 2014 attack card appears as the character and CritAssist can observe its natural 1; AttackAssist leaves damage and resources for the table to resolve.

During travel, the GM advances TimeAlmanac, selects the active climate region, and generates current Weather. Astronomy contributes the campaign's moon phases and daylight while EnviroAlmanac turns the committed conditions into concise visibility, temperature, wind, ground, water, exposure, and severity context. At camp, RestAlmanac previews every selected 2014 PC and proposed sheet change before a confirmed rest; fictional time advances only when that choice was part of the preview.

When everyone is ready, the GM starts CombatAssist. A single custom row named Round, Rounds, Round Count, Round Counter, Round Number, Round Tracker, Combat Round, or Current Round becomes the round authority; when CombatAssist moves that row to the top, a simple signed whole-number calculation such as `+1` is honored. Without one, a full uninterrupted forward cycle advances CombatAssist's internal round and a backward step never does. Optional timers can remind the GM, current player, both, or public chat without advancing initiative, while native pings can briefly identify the current token without changing it. The GM can also recover the last readable tracker, pause for several quiet edits, or use `!Combat-Next` and `!Combat-Prev` for guarded one-step movement.

## 💬 Main Commands

### System and Configuration

- `!ga-status` — Show overall health, module state, errors, and dependency information
- `!ga-status --details` — Add activity, listener, timing, shared-service, and overlap diagnostics
- `!ga-health` / `!ga-health recent` / `!ga-health audit` — Review HealthService status, bounded recent HP evidence, or supported tokens on the Player Ribbon page
- `!ga-health bars` — Choose Bar 1, 2, or 3 for shared NPC HP, audit current-page setup, and prepare linked NPC tokens
- `!ga-health alerts` — Manage optional GM-private 50%, 25%, and 10% PC health notices, exact-HP visibility, and a safe preview
- `!ga-config ui` or `!ga-config-ui` — Open the GM configuration panel
- `!ConfigUI-GM` or `!ConfigUI-DM` — Open ConfigUI's private Game Master screen
- `!ga-config modules` — List feature modules, core services, and their current status
- `!ga-config list` — Write a versioned configuration-only snapshot handout
- `!ga-config get <ModuleOrService> [key]` / `!ga-config set <ModuleOrService> <key>=<value>` — Review or change component configuration
- `!ga-enable <ModuleOrService>` / `!ga-disable <ModuleOrService>` — Enable or disable a feature module or core service
- `!ga-metrics` — Show GameAssist runtime metrics

### Critical Misses

- `!critfumble help` — Open the CritAssist quick-reference guide
- `!critfumble menu` — Open the guided Natural 1 menu
- `!CritAssist-GM` or `!CritAssist-DM` — Open CritAssist's private Game Master player picker
- `!critfail` — Open the direct manual player picker
- `!critfumble-<melee|ranged|thrown|spell|natural>` — Roll the selected fumble table
- `!confirm-crit-martial` / `!confirm-crit-magic` — Roll confirmation tables

### Conditions

- `!condition` — Open the selected-token condition menu
- `!Condition-GM` or `!Condition-DM` — Open ConditionAssist's private selected-token Game Master screen
- `!condition help` — Open the quick-start guide
- `!condition status` — List current-page characters and NPCs with configured conditions or other active markers
- `!condition <name>` or `!cond-<condition>` — Show one configured condition description
- `!condition add|remove|toggle <condition...>` — Change condition markers on selected tokens when permitted
- `!condition announce`, `!c-a`, or `!cond-!` — Toggle a condition marker, then report who is or is no longer affected
- `!condition config` — Choose 2014 SRD, 2024 SRD, or campaign-custom wording and open definitions or validated import/export

### Token Controls

- `!TokenAssist-GM` or `!TokenAssist-DM` — Open TokenAssist's private selected-token control screen
- `!token-assist help` or `!ta-help` — Open the TokenAssist quick guide
- `!token-assist about` or `!ta-about` — Review attribution, supported behavior, and current limits
- `!token-assist config` or `!ta-config` — Manage explicit player-ID targeting
- `!ta-on|off|flip <property...>` — Change supported token switches
- `!ta-set <property|value...>` — Change supported token values, auras, or status markers
- `!ta-move`, `!ta-order`, or `!ta-report` — Move, stack, or report on targeted tokens
- `!ta-ids <token-or-character-id...>` — Target explicit IDs when authorized
- `!token-assist --<action> ...` — Use the same actions with the full command name
- `!token-mod ...` — Retained compatibility syntax; use `!token-assist` or `!ta` for new macros

### Initiative

- `!Init-Help` / `!Init-Menu` — Open the InitiativeAssist Guide or action-focused Control Center
- `!Init-Go` / `!Init-Go!` — Publicly invite players to roll, then whisper the GM a PC/NPC roster with individual and batch controls
- `!Init-GM` / `!Init-DM` — Whisper the GM the neutral roll controls and complete roster without posting an invitation
- `!Init-Roll` / `!Init-Options` — Roll a controlled character with cumulative d20, flat-adjustment, and bonus-die choices
- `!Init-Roll-Selected` — Roll every eligible selected character controlled by the clicking GM or player
- `!Init-Start --scope all|npc|gm-npc|all-npc` — Roll object-layer characters, object-layer NPCs, GM-layer NPCs, or NPCs across both layers
- `!Init-NPC-Rolls hidden|public` — Choose whether object-layer NPC evidence is GM-only; GM-layer evidence always stays private
- `!Init-RR` — Reroll every eligible PC and living NPC already in the tracker and whisper the result summary to the GM
- `!Init-RR-Menu` — Choose PCs, NPCs, selected tokens, individuals, or saved groups
- `!Init-Status` / `!Init-Audit` — Open the quick Status Summary or the detailed read-only GM chat review
- `!Init-Mode observer|manager` — Choose read-only coexistence or InitiativeAssist-owned writes

### Combat

- `!Combat-GM` / `!Combat-DM` — Open the private CombatAssist Control Center
- `!Combat-Menu` / `!Combat-Help` — Open the action-focused Control Center or plain-language Quick Guide
- `!Combat-Start` / `!Combat-Start --confirm` — Begin round 1, or deliberately replace an existing encounter baseline
- `!Combat-Next` / `!Combat-Prev` — Move the native Turn Tracker forward or backward by exactly one row through GameAssist's guarded tracker service
- `!Combat-End-Turn --token <ID>` — Generated player control in Whispers mode; advances only if the clicking player still controls the current character
- `!Combat-Adopt` / `!Combat-Restore` — Keep the current readable tracker or preview and confirm a one-step restoration of the last accepted tracker
- `!Combat-Pause` / `!Combat-Resume` — Optionally pause while making several tracker edits, then resume without changing the round
- `!Combat-Status` — Review the round, current turn, tracking state, and any action that needs attention
- `!Combat-End` / `!Combat-End --confirm` — Clear only CombatAssist's encounter record and leave all tracker rows unchanged
- `!Combat-Announce gm|public|whispers|off` — Choose GM-only, public, separate GM/current-player whispers, or no automatic turn announcements
- `!Combat-Confirm standard|varied` — Choose one direct message or a restrained rotation of private acknowledgements after a player ends a turn
- `!Combat-Timer` — Configure turn length, deadline recipients, and up to five early reminders; timers never advance initiative
- `!Combat-Cue off|gm|players|both|public` — Configure Roll20's temporary native current-turn ping without changing token properties or map position

### WelcomeAssist

- `!Welcome-GM` / `!Welcome-DM` — Open WelcomeAssist's private setup and status screen
- `!Welcome` / `!Welcome-Help` — Open the guide
- `!Welcome-Status` / `!Welcome-Preview` — Review configuration or preview privately
- `!Welcome-Announce` — Post one greeting publicly now
- `!Welcome-Mode default|builtin|custom|mixed` — Choose the greeting pool
- `!Welcome-Delay <seconds>` — Set the startup delay from 1 to 60 seconds
- `!Welcome-Header show|hide|<text>` — Control the greeting header
- `!Welcome-Custom list|add|remove|clear` — Manage campaign greetings

The longer `!welcome-assist ...` forms remain accepted for existing macros.

### Concentration

- `!Con-GM` / `!Con-DM` or `!Concentration-GM` / `!Concentration-DM` — Open the private ConcentrationAssist Game Master screen
- `!concentration` or `!cc` — Open concentration-check buttons
- `!Con-<command>` and `!Concentration-<command>` — Equivalent case-insensitive command families for the module controls below
- `!concentration --damage <amount> --mode <normal|adv|dis>` — Roll a concentration save
- `!concentration --last` — Repeat the player's previous check
- `!concentration --off` — Remove the configured marker from selected linked tokens
- `!concentration --status` — List concentrating tokens on the page marked by Roll20's Player Ribbon
- `!ga-conc-status` — Show the GM concentration activity summary
- `!concentration settings` — Choose result-message style, private HP-loss check offers, and the campaign concentration marker\n- `!concentration markers` / `!concentration marker --value <name-or-tag>` — Choose a built-in or registered custom marker through the GM interface

### NPC History and Reporting

- `!NPC-GM`, `!NPC-Death-GM`, or `!NPCAssist-GM` — Open the private NPCAssist Game Master screen; each also accepts `-DM`
- `!NPC-<command>`, `!NPC-Death-<command>`, and `!NPCAssist-<command>` — Equivalent case-insensitive NPCAssist command families
- `!npc-death-report --help` or `!npc-death-help` — Open the central NPCAssist guide
- `!npc-death-report [--scope campaign|chapter|section|session] [--recent|--page N|--write]` — Review a reporting scope or open the report writer
- `!npc-death-buckets` — Review or rename active reporting scopes
- `!npc-death-write` or `!npc-wr` — Write NPC history to handouts
- `!npc-death-audit` — Check HP and death-marker consistency without changing tokens, then update the audit handout
- `!npc-death-repair` — Preview marker corrections from current HP and require confirmation before changing only the configured death marker
- `!npc-death-arc` — Create and manage custom Arc rosters from selected tokens or the current Session
- `!npc-death-clear [--scope campaign|chapter|section|session] [--nested] [--confirm]` — Clear records using explicit confirmation

### Effects

- `!Effect-GM`, `!Effect-DM`, or `!Effect-Menu` — Open EffectAssist's private Game Master controls
- `!effect` or `!Effect-Catalog` — Open the focused catalog directly; automated entries are separated from tracked/manual entries
- `!Bless`, `!Guidance` / `!Guide`, `!Haste`, `!Warding-Bond`, `!Holy-Weapon`, or `!PwoaT` — Open a compact player-safe source-and-review path
- `!Effect-Active` / `!Effect-Status` / `!Effect-Definitions` — Manage active sources, review compact health totals, or inspect catalog details
- `!Effect-Requests` — Review retained player requests for recipients that require GM assistance
- `!Effect-Casts` / `!Effect-Recognition on|off` — Review supported official 2014 Bless proposals or turn this private GM shortcut on or off
- `!Effect-Duration` / `!Effect-Durations on|off` — Review duration evidence or turn new duration candidates on or off; elapsed time never ends an effect automatically
- `!Effect-Players on|off` — Allow or lock player casting from controlled linked sources
- `!Effect-Audit` — Compare semantic records against exact markers, conditions, concentration state, and 2014-sheet rows without changing anything
- `!Effect-Manual` — Create or update the stable EffectAssist manual handout
- `!Effect-End --id <generated-id>` — End one exact source instance through generated buttons and remove only unneeded owned state
- `!Effect-Guide` / `!Effect-Help` / `!Effect-Info` / `!effect <command>` — Open guidance or use the same case-insensitive controls through the spaced command family

### Healing

- `!Heal-Max` — Open maximum healing for supported spells, potions, and formulas
- `!Heal-Auto on|off` — Choose automatic verified application or the default review-before-apply workflow
- `!Heal-GM` or `!Heal-DM` — Open the private Game Master controls
- `!Heal-Guide` / `!Heal-Help` / `!Heal-Info` / `!Heal-Manual` — Open guidance, boundaries, or the stable manual handout

## 🔄 Working Alongside Other Mods

GameAssist is designed to share a campaign with unrelated Roll20 Mods. Problems arise when two enabled tools respond to the same command, control the same token property, or react to the same event.

- **General token controls:** TokenAssist uses `!token-assist` and `!ta`/`!ta-*`. Older `!token-mod` syntax is left to standalone TokenMod when that script is detected. Remove standalone TokenMod for normal v2.0.0 use because both tools can still change the same token properties and markers.
- **Conditions:** Standalone StatusInfo overlaps ConditionAssist's `!condition` commands and marker descriptions. Remove it when ConditionAssist is enabled.
- **Initiative and Turn Tracker:** Another initiative roller or combat manager may rewrite the same character turns, add round rows, advance turns, count rounds, or announce the same encounter. Use one initiative writer and one encounter-flow owner for a given encounter: InitiativeAssist can use Observer mode, and CombatAssist can remain disabled. GameAssist preserves custom tracker rows but cannot prevent another Mod from changing them later.
- **NPC HP and token bars:** Another Mod that automatically rolls, replaces, damages, heals, or synchronizes GameAssist's selected NPC HP bar can trigger HP, Bloodied-notice, and death-history workflows. Choose one tool to own automatic NPC HP changes, or disable the overlapping feature. The 5th Edition OGL by Roll20 Companion `!npchp` and automatic NPC-token options are examples of this overlap.
- **5th Edition OGL Companion attacks:** The supplied Companion handler ignores API-originated attack templates, so AttackAssist rolls should not spend its ammunition or spell slots; normal Classic-sheet clicks still may. Confirm both behaviors once with disposable attacks after changing either script.
- **Status markers and effect projections:** Another Mod that automatically changes the same death, concentration, condition, or EffectAssist projection marker can compete with GameAssist and produce confusing results. Assign one automation tool to each marker or projection.
- **Natural 1 attack handling:** Another Mod that watches the same attack templates for natural 1s can produce duplicate menus or multiple fumble results. Keep only one automatic critical-miss workflow enabled.
- **Guided attack submission:** Another Mod or macro that automatically submits the same repeating attack or announces the same attacker and target can create duplicate rolls or messages. Use one guided attack workflow for that sheet action.
- **Startup greetings:** Another Mod that automatically posts a campaign-ready or welcome message may produce duplicate table announcements. Disable one automatic greeting when the combined output is unwanted.
- **GameAssist report handouts:** Report, audit, Arc, and configuration handouts are regenerated from GameAssist data when their write commands run. Keep unrelated campaign notes in separate handouts so they are not replaced.

These cautions concern overlapping behavior, not the mere presence of another Mod. Lighting, maps, macros, character utilities, and automation that does not also own GameAssist's token, marker, HP, fumble, or Turn Tracker responsibilities can continue normally.

## 🛡️ Safeguards You Can See

- Newly added NPC tokens receive a short setup window so placeholder HP does not create a false death, revival, or Bloodied notice.
- Eligible living object-layer NPCs can privately alert the GM when they cross to half HP or below; the notice never reveals NPC HP publicly or adds marker/history state.
- TokenAssist validates a command before changing token properties and refuses unsupported features without applying the other requested changes.
- Every TokenAssist status operation uses MarkerService, including built-in, numbered, custom-name, and exact-tag markers.
- Built-in and custom markers are matched to the exact marker Roll20 stores on the token, and ConditionAssist displays marker artwork when Roll20 exposes it.
- `!npc-death-audit` creates or updates a dedicated handout listing NPCs that need attention without changing tokens.
- `!npc-death-repair` separately previews, confirms, re-scans, and verifies death-marker corrections while preserving HP and history.
- Named table timezones follow daylight-saving changes while stored event instants remain absolute.
- TurnTrackerService resolves both page-id and open-tracker campaign states while preserving unknown fields and non-owned rows. GameAssist-created token turns include Roll20's encounter-page field, use a dedicated Turn Order update, and are verified before InitiativeAssist or CombatAssist reports success. NPC inline rolls and result panels respect the GM's privacy setting, and GM-layer NPC evidence is never posted publicly.
- CombatAssist begins only when the GM starts it, uses one unambiguous native round-counter row when present, otherwise counts only proven complete forward cycles, preserves valid native lineup and initiative changes without resetting the round, and retains one confirmed recovery checkpoint. Timer callbacks recheck the exact encounter, round, current token, tracker revision, and deadline before sending anything; they never advance initiative. Current-turn pings use Roll20's temporary ping and never overwrite token markers, auras, tints, or positions. Its GM turn panels include Next Turn, Previous Turn, and Open Menu; Whispers mode separately gives the current controlling player an authorization-checked End My Turn button and private completion notice. TurnTrackerService is required. An optional integration may require another GameAssist component; when that component is unavailable, only the integration is unavailable and both modules keep their normal independent features.
- EffectAssist keeps semantic records separate from marker, condition, concentration, and 2014-sheet projections; binds concentration to the exact chosen source token; identifies invalid recipients precisely; preserves and reports pre-existing state; refuses to delete externally edited rows; uses sheet workers for supported activation and cleanup; and verifies writes. Player casting revalidates the current player and controlled source, visible recipients use Roll20's target picker, stale buttons provide a clear restart, and hidden recipient names are not announced publicly. GM placement requests remain available briefly in `!Effect-Requests`; cast recognition and elapsed duration produce review choices rather than automatic application or cleanup.
- HealAssist supports normal or maximum healing, caps healing at maximum HP, revalidates recipients, verifies every accepted HealthService write, and refuses stale or reused confirmation buttons. Review-before-apply remains the default; automatic mode privately reports a failed write to the GM. It never spends spell slots, items, class resources, or temporary HP.
- AttackAssist verifies the authorized 2014 source and exact repeating row, uses the Classic sheet's documented defaults when unchanged checkboxes were never persisted, uses Roll20 targeting for visible tokens, keeps hidden placement private, consumes each reviewed roll once, and never applies attack consequences or changes encounter state.
- AlmanacAssist keeps one signed fictional chronology separate from the table timezone and NPCAssist Session dates. Year 1 remains the saved-campaign anchor while Year 0 is represented without shifting existing dates. One immutable SceneResolver supplies coherent current conditions and provenance. Destination, travel, temporal-context, preset, Wayfarer, and WorldPack previews change nothing until their exact confirmation; stale or malformed handouts cause no partial import. Runtime chronology and character state are excluded from WorldPacks, imported calendars remain unreviewed drafts, Environment applies no automatic penalties, RulesAdvisor is read-only, and Rest revalidates supported 2014-sheet fields immediately before one confirmed transaction.
- SemanticEvents provides immutable, versioned, in-sandbox notifications for optional integrations without persisting, replaying, or silently enabling providers.
- HealthService deduplicates supported linked sheet/token HP evidence, verifies GameAssist-owned HP writes, and gives the GM one shared Bar 1/2/3 selection plus current-page NPC setup and unlinked-token auditing. Optional PC health alerts combine downward threshold crossings into one GM-only notice, hide exact HP by default, and never overlap NPCAssist NPC policy. ConcentrationAssist may offer a private check after a supported decrease, but an unexplained change remains labeled **Observed HP Loss** and never becomes a claimed attacker, damage type, or automatic concentration result.
- Every DebugTools action is a dry run until the GM includes `--apply`.
- MarkerService can be disabled when another Mod must own marker behavior. GameAssist first disables ConditionAssist, TokenAssist, NPCAssist, ConcentrationAssist, and DebugTools, while CritAssist, ConfigUI, InitiativeAssist, WelcomeAssist, and HPAssist remain available.
- TurnTrackerService can be disabled when another Mod must own native tracker behavior. InitiativeAssist and CombatAssist are disabled first, and the current Roll20 tracker is left unchanged.
- WelcomeAssist starts disabled, previews privately, waits for healthy GameAssist startup, neutralizes Roll20 directives in campaign text, and automatically posts at most once per sandbox lifecycle.

## 🩺 Troubleshooting

Start with `!ga-status`, then use `!ga-status --details` and `!ga-config modules`. For supported HP evidence, use `!ga-health`, `!ga-health recent`, and the read-only `!ga-health audit`; use `!ga-health bars` for shared NPC HP setup and `!ga-health alerts` to review PC threshold settings and send a harmless preview. Open `!ga-nav`, choose the affected module, and use its direct settings, help, Enable, or Disable action before changing persistent state or enabling DebugTools. For initiative, use `!Init-Status` and `!Init-Audit`; for encounter flow, use `!Combat-Status`, use Restore when a recent tracker edit must be undone, and verify Whispers mode with a separate non-GM player login; for table greetings, use `!Welcome-Status` and `!Welcome-Preview`; for effects, use `!Effect-Status`, `!Effect-Requests`, `!Effect-Casts`, `!Effect-Duration`, and the read-only `!Effect-Audit`; for attacks, use `!Attack-Status`, `!Attack-Requests`, and the read-only `!Attack-Audit`; for world context or rests, use `!Almanac-Status` and the read-only `!Almanac-Audit`; unreadable 2024 data, dead or mismatched NPCs, stale tokens, and custom rows are intentionally identified instead of guessed. If an initiative result appears without a Turn Order row, reopen the tracker on the encounter page and retry.

> MarkerService should appear enabled when marker-dependent modules are in use. Test a real death, concentration marker, condition cycle, and harmless selected-token command on disposable tokens before relying on a new installation.
